sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Lily of the valley is a rhizomatous Eurasian perennial, usually 15–25 cm tall. Its underground rhizomes spread to form colonies; two basal leaves surround a flowering stem with a one-sided cluster of white bells.

sections.title: Fruit and toxicity
sections.text: Red berries may develop after flowering. The whole plant is toxic if eaten, including the berries, leaves, flowers and roots; it contains cardiac glycosides. The plate correctly shows the two leaves, bell-shaped flower cluster and berries.
